1. (Currently amended) A method comprising:
receiving requests and data records from a plurality of creditors to file bankruptcy documents with a plurality of different bankruptcy organizations, wherein the bankruptcy documents are proofs of claim forms for debts owed by debtors to the creditors;
automatically generating the bankruptcy documents with the received data records, wherein the bankruptcy documents are suitable for filing with different bankruptcy organizations and include supporting documentation specific to each bankruptcy organization's requirements; and
batch filing the bankruptcy documents with the different bankruptcy organizations via electronic submission to court filing systems.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the different bankruptcy organizations are different courts with different filing system configurations, and wherein the automatically generating step comprises transforming a single data record into multiple court-specific document formats.

6. (Currently amended) A method comprising:
receiving requests from a plurality of creditors to file proofs of claims for debts owed by debtors to the creditors with a plurality of different bankruptcy organizations, wherein each request includes a data record for generating a proof of claim and the proofs of claims include both claim forms and supporting documentation;
automatically generating the proofs of claims with the received data records, wherein the proofs of claims are suitable for filing with different bankruptcy organizations and are formatted according to each bankruptcy organization's specific filing requirements; and
batch filing the proofs of claims with the different bankruptcy organizations via electronic submission to court filing systems.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein the different bankruptcy organizations are different bankruptcy courts having different filing system configurations, and wherein the automatically generating step comprises transforming a single creditor data record into multiple court-specific proof of claim formats.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 further comprising sending bankruptcy notification messages to the plurality of creditors, wherein the bankruptcy notification messages notify the creditors of the filing status of their proofs of claims with specific bankruptcy courts.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein receiving requests from the plurality of creditors comprises receiving the requests using a secure file transfer protocol and validating the data records prior to generating the proofs of claims.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein receiving requests comprises receiving requests via a Web site with user authentication and encryption.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 where batch filing comprises aggregating the proofs of claims by bankruptcy court and filing the proofs of claims in a batch mode at least once per day with electronic confirmation of filing.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 further comprising:
generating a report specific to each creditor showing the status of their filed proofs of claims; and
sending the report to a particular creditor via secure electronic transmission.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 wherein generating the report comprises enabling a user to request the report using a Web site with user authentication.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 wherein generating the report comprises generating an aging report specifying a reason some proofs of claims have not been filed and the status of pending filings with specific bankruptcy courts.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 further comprising receiving a filing receipt for a filed proof of claim from the bankruptcy court.

16. (Original) The method of claim 6 wherein batch filing is performed by a server computer.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 further comprising validating the data record against bankruptcy court filing requirements prior to generating the proofs of claims.
